scenes.headline: How a model learns coarse-to-real without paired videos
scenes.sub: Pairs of still images stand in for pairs of videos
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Selvage! This method turns rough renders into realistic video, and it never saw a rough video with its real twin.

scenes.text: Paired videos are expensive, but paired still images are cheap. Learn real to coarse on images, and run it on real video to fake the pairs.
scenes.mark: run it on real video to fake the pairs
scenes.say: Pairs of videos are costly. Pairs of still images are cheap. So learn real to coarse on images, then run it on real video to fake the pairs.

steps.say: A DINO network learns from still image pairs to predict how a realistic picture looks when coarse.
Run it on every frame of ordinary real videos and you get a coarse version of each, already paired.
Decode those features to pixels and encode them again, so only what a coarse picture can hold gets through.
The adapters learn to regenerate the real video from that control, on a frozen video model.
The top row is the bridge. It trains on image pairs, then runs on video frames.
The bottom row trains the video model, then at inference a real coarse video replaces the fake one.

left.title: Raw features
items: Keep traces of the real picture
Training sees hints that test lacks
left.say: Raw predicted features keep traces of the real picture that a true coarse video never has.

right.title: Decode, re-encode
right.say: Decoding to pixels and encoding again removes those traces, so training looks like testing.

scenes.label: toy error with and without the decode step, 20 image pairs
scenes.note: my toy, not the paper's model
scenes.say: In my small toy, with twenty image pairs, skipping the decode step raised the error from point zero three five to point one two seven.

scenes.text: The bridge turns cheap image pairs into video pairs, but its output must look like real coarse input, not like a leak.
scenes.mark: must look like real coarse input
scenes.say: The bridge turns cheap image pairs into video pairs. What matters is that its output looks like real coarse input.

recap: Learn real to coarse on images.
Swap in real coarse at inference.
scenes.say: Learn on images, fake the pairs from real video, and swap in the real coarse video at the end.
